title: Getting Around
grammarNote: This lesson covers usted affirmative imperatives for giving directions (siga, dé vuelta, tome, baje, cruce), prepositions of place (enfrente de, a la derecha de, entre, hasta), and the use of estar (never ser) for location. It's built around asking for and following directions on foot, by Metro, and by camión in Mexico City.

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Siga' is the usted affirmative imperative of seguir (to continue/follow), the standard polite command for giving directions to a stranger.

exampleSentence.target: Siga derecho dos cuadras y va a ver la plaza.
exampleSentence.native: Go straight two blocks and you'll see the plaza.

phrases.grammarNote: Usted commands use the same form as the usted present subjunctive: seguir → siga (e→i stem change), dropping the -o and adding -a for -ir verbs.
phrases.memoryHook: Siga sounds like 'see-ga' — SEE where you're GOing and keep moving straight.

practiceItems.prompt: Un turista te pide indicaciones y debe caminar derecho por dos cuadras. ¿Qué le dices?

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Dé vuelta' is the usted imperative of dar + vuelta ('give a turn'), the standard phrase for telling someone to turn at an intersection.

exampleSentence.target: En el semáforo, dé vuelta a la derecha.
exampleSentence.native: At the traffic light, turn right.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Dé' is the irregular usted imperative of dar, written with an accent to distinguish it from the preposition 'de'; it's always followed by 'vuelta' plus a direction.
phrases.memoryHook: Dé vuelta = 'give a turn' — picture handing the wheel a little turn to the right.

practiceItems.prompt: En el semáforo, ___ vuelta a la derecha.
Le explicas a alguien que debe girar hacia la derecha en el semáforo. ¿Qué le dices?

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Tome' is the usted imperative of tomar (to take), used both for taking transportation and for physically taking an object; 'camión' is the common Mexican word for a city bus.

exampleSentence.target: Tome el camión número diez hasta el centro.
exampleSentence.native: Take bus number ten to downtown.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Tomar' is a regular -ar verb, so the usted imperative simply swaps the -ar ending for -e: tomar → tome.
phrases.memoryHook: Tome sounds like 'toe-may' — TOE the line and get on the right bus.

practiceItems.prompt: Necesitas decirle a alguien qué camión debe abordar para llegar al centro. ¿Qué le dices?

phrases.native: Get off at the next stop
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Baje' is the usted imperative of bajar (to get off/descend), commonly used on buses and the Metro to tell a passenger where to disembark.

exampleSentence.target: Baje en la siguiente parada y camine dos cuadras.
exampleSentence.native: Get off at the next stop and walk two blocks.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Bajar' is a regular -ar verb; its usted imperative follows the same pattern as tomar → tome, swapping -ar for -e: bajar → baje.
phrases.memoryHook: Baje sounds like 'bah-hey' — say 'hey, I'm getting off' as you step down.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Get off at the next stop
Le indicas a un pasajero en qué parada debe descender del camión. ¿Qué le dices?

phrases.target: El museo está enfrente de la estación
phrases.native: The museum is in front of the station
phrases.phonetic: el moo-SEH-oh es-TAH en-FREN-teh deh lah es-tah-see-ON
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Estar' (not ser) is used with location, and 'enfrente de' means 'in front of' or 'across from' — a common preposition of place for giving directions.

exampleSentence.target: El museo está enfrente de la estación del Metro.
exampleSentence.native: The museum is in front of the Metro station.

phrases.grammarNote: Location always takes estar, never ser: 'el museo está' (is located), not 'el museo es'. 'Enfrente de' requires 'de' before the noun it refers to.
phrases.memoryHook: Enfrente sounds like 'in front' — en-FRENT-e, picture standing right in front.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: The museum is in front of the station
practiceItems.answer: El museo está enfrente de la estación

practiceItems.prompt: El museo ___ enfrente de la estación.
Alguien te pregunta dónde está el museo en relación con la estación del Metro. ¿Qué le dices?
practiceItems.answer: El museo está enfrente de la estación

dialogue.scenario: You ask a stranger how to reach the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Mexico City.

turns.speaker: npc
turns.native: Hello, how can I help you?

turns.speaker: npc
turns.line: Siga derecho dos cuadras y dé vuelta a la derecha.
turns.native: Go straight two blocks and turn right.

turns.speaker: npc
turns.line: Así es. Luego cruce la calle y tome el camión número diez.
turns.native: That's right. Then cross the street and take bus number ten.

turns.speaker: npc
turns.line: Baje en la siguiente parada; el museo está enfrente de la estación.
turns.native: Get off at the next stop; the museum is in front of the station.
